messages:
maya: Heads up — promotion scheduled tonight 22:00 UTC for chart ai-serving -> prod (v2.3.0). Staging canary flagged two compatibility warnings: values overlay changed tenantPVCName (can break PV binding) and CRD schema strictness for /status. /cc @tom @linh

 tom: can you paste the helm diff or exact values snippet?

 maya: sure, from the canary run:```diff
- pvcName: ai-serving-tenant-{{ .Values.tenant }}
+ pvcName: ai-serving-{{ .Values.tenant }}-data

# also values.enabled.migrations.job = true -> now set to migrations.runOnUpgradeOnly
```

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary deployment started for ai-serving:2.3.0 in staging (canary 3/10). health checks passing so far, but warning emitted by admission-webhook: CRD.status field strict schema mismatch.

 linh: that pvc rename is a big red flag for prod mounts. If the claim name changes the binding may not find the PV. We should avoid promoting until we run the migration job that renames claims or preserves PVs. Suggest pin to 2.2.7 and re-run canary after the migration test.

 andrew: I'll take release notes. If we pin, we must ensure the pinned image digest is in the chart values (no floating tags). Also add an explicit rollback section in notes.

 sophie: Also saw the admission webhook in eu-west will reject the new CRD payload unless disableStrictSchemas is set in the chart (we added stricter schema in 2.3.0). We can add a temporary values override to bypass until webhooks are updated, but that is risky.

 maya: decision proposed: PAUSE promotion. Manual pin to chart v2.2.7 and open tracking ticket. Plan: 1) abort current promotion, 2) pin chart in release manifest + include image digest, 3) run migration job on dev and staging (validate PV bind), 4) re-run canary with overlay disableStrictSchemas=true for eu-west, 5) if green proceed. Any objections?

 tom: +1. I'll prepare the pin PR and include the helm commands.

 tom:```bash
# pin to previous chart and annotate rollback reason
helm upgrade ai-serving myrepo/ai-serving --version 2.2.7 --set image.tag=sha256:abcdef123456 --namespace prod \
  --atomic --wait --description "pin-to-2.2.7 due to pvc rename/CRD schema"
# annotate release for audit
kubectl annotate deploy/ai-serving release-pin=2.2.7 -n prod || true
```

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary aborted at 3/10 per manual hold requested by maya. Rollback to previous release in staging scheduled in 5m.

 andrew: I'll add a breaking-change bullet in the notes: "PVC name template changed; see migration job INF-4321 for remediation steps." Also include quick rollback commands: `kubectl rollout undo deployment/ai-serving -n prod` and `kubectl rollout restart deployment/ai-serving -n prod` for post-rollback reconciliation.

 linh: I'll run the migration sanity on dev cluster and post results here in ~45m. Will validate PV binding and run the migration job with a snapshot.

 maya: thanks. I'll update the release calendar and notify support + account teams. Creating INF-4321 now and linking it.

 maya: INF-4321 created: https://jira.redwood/INF-4321 — title: "ai-serving chart 2.3.0 pvc-name change + CRD schema: hold and migration"

 deploy-bot: deploy-bot: rollback executed in staging to ai-serving:2.2.7 (image sha256:abcdef123456). Canary state: halted. Logs: pod ai-serving-6789 started with previous PVC binding intact.

 sophie: good catch. once linh posts validation we can decide whether to (a) patch chart to support both PVC name patterns for one release, (b) run a data-preserving migration job, or (c) push a minor bump that keeps naming backwards compatible. I'm leaning (a) as fastest.

 maya: agreed. we'll prefer backward-compatible patch for the next patch release, then follow up with a planned breaking bump in a minor release after migration tooling is GA. I'll assign follow-ups in INF-4321.

 andrew: I'll hold public release notes and add an internal advisory to accounts about the hold.

 tom: PR for pin opened: https://git.redwood/infra/helm-charts/pulls/4523 — includes helm upgrade command and changelog note.

 maya: thanks everyone. will re-open thread when dev migration results are in. :white_check_mark:
